teaser.text: Becton Dickinson (BD) sells the physical tools and systems that let healthcare workers give treatment, collect samples, monitor patients, and perform procedures. Its business is a loop: customers buy products and equipment, BD supplies follow-on consumables and support, and the cash left after making and serving them can fund further investment.

stock.title: BD stock forecast
stock.meta_description: BD's weighted forecast reaches $265.17 in October 2029 across bear, base and bull scenarios.
stock.opening: BD's weighted forecast points to $265.17 in October 2029. It hinges on turning a repaired Alaris base and GLP-1 programs into durable earnings, margin and cash-flow growth.
stock.closing: The full BD memo also explains BD's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could BD's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast points to $219.78 in October 2027 and $241.89 in October 2028. It reaches $265.17 in October 2029. Including dividends, those prices imply returns of 17% and 31% at the first two dates. The three-year return is 45%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for BD?

paragraphs.text: The bear case holds earnings near $3.4 billion because quality actions, pricing pressure, tariffs and weak vaccine demand offset growth. The bull case reaches $3,940 million first and $4,995 million last because GLP-1 programs scale, execution improves and margins expand. Recent adjusted EPS growth and seven consecutive analyst beats support the base, but the lack of detailed launch conversion limits confidence in the bull case.

blocks.heading: How much cash does BD really make?

paragraphs.text: BD generated $3.430 billion from continuing operating activities in fiscal 2025, down from $3.844 billion in fiscal 2024. It spent $760 million on capital expenditures in fiscal 2025, mainly on manufacturing capacity, leaving simple free cash flow of about $2.670 billion before acquisitions, dividends, debt repayment and buybacks. The dividend was $1.196 billion in fiscal 2025, so operating cash after capital spending covered it.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for BD today?

paragraphs.text: Market value is what shareholders collectively own. Enterprise value estimates what it would cost to own the operating business, including the lenders’ claim. It adds debt and subtracts cash because a buyer would inherit the debt but receive the cash. Using June 30, 2026 balances, BD had US$16.808 billion of debt and about US$0.863 billion of cash, short-term investments, and restricted cash. The difference shows why the business must satisfy both shareholders and lenders.

The two P/E measures use different earnings periods. P/E means the share price divided by earnings per share. BD reported diluted EPS of US$1.64 and adjusted EPS of US$3.23 in Q3 FY2026. Amortization is an accounting charge that spreads the cost of acquired assets over time; adjusted EPS removes selected charges, so it can clarify operations but is neither GAAP earnings nor cash.

dividend.title: BD dividend: payout, cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: BD dividend payout history, cash coverage, risks and current yield explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: BD paid $4.15 dividends per share in FY2025. Its $1.196 billion dividend was covered by about $2.670 billion of free cash flow after capital spending.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains BD’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does BD pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: FY2025 revenue rose 10.2%, but operating margin was 10.5%; growth has yet to become stronger reported profitability. Diluted EPS was $3.81 against $4.15 dividends paid per share, while the average diluted share count fell 0.9% after rising 0.9% in FY2024. Net debt was $18,604 million. Valuation is 50.5x trailing P/E and 14.5x next-twelve-month P/E; shareholder yields are 2.2% from dividends and 1.9% from buybacks.

Dividends begin from the indicated $4.20 annual rate. The base case reaches $4.24 in 2027 and $4.32 in 2029 through one-cent quarterly increases. The bear case pauses at $4.20 before reaching $4.24, while the bull case reaches $4.52 through faster increases. The 54-year increase record supports continued growth, but debt and remediation argue for caution.

earnings.meta_description: BD's next results are expected November 5, 2026, with guidance focused on low single-digit growth, adjusted EPS and operating margin.
earnings.opening: BD's next results are expected on November 5, 2026. Watch Alaris remediation and its effect on sales and cash flow.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains BD's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has BD guided for FY2026?

paragraphs.text: Management’s August outlook calls for low single-digit FX-neutral revenue growth, meaning growth measured without exchange-rate changes. Its adjusted diluted EPS target excludes selected costs such as amortization and legal charges, while adjusted operating margin measures operating profit left from each sales dollar after those adjustments. A currency tailwind can lift reported sales even when underlying demand is unchanged. One basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point, so basis points give a precise way to describe small margin movements.

blocks.heading: What has BD's revenue and profit done recently?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose from June 2025 to June 2026. Gross margin fell over the same comparison, and operating income also declined. Net income was unchanged, while diluted EPS increased. That divergence means financing, tax and share-count effects improved the per-share result even though operating profitability weakened.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in BD's next results?

paragraphs.text: Alaris is BD’s infusion-pump system for delivering fluids and medicines in hospitals. Remediation means repairing, replacing or updating devices already in use. BD says U.S. pumps are being remediated or replaced with an updated cleared version, with the work expected to be substantially complete in calendar 2026. Completion should reduce execution risk, but management expects it to create about a 200-basis-point revenue-growth headwind in FY27 because replacement activity will no longer boost comparisons.
BD’s Q4 and FY26 results call on November 5 should put numbers around Alaris, tariffs, China and vaccines. Investors should also watch corrective actions, sterilization rules and related claims.
